LESSON: GUIDED READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: READING Theme 5: Fun and Enjoyment: My Birthday
Topic 2.5: Guided reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you love reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify information from reading texts
2. appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading
3. read out words with the correct pronunciation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided reading helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify information from reading texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify information from reading texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify information from reading texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify information from reading texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Read out words with the correct pronunciation

What this means
In this part you learn to read out words with the correct pronunciation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read out words with the correct pronunciation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read out words with the correct pronunciation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify information from reading texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided reading to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: read out words with the correct pronunciation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify information from reading texts.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading.
4. Practise this skill: read out words with the correct pronunciation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Guided reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you love reading?
2. When do you read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify information from reading texts.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
